Question: Can every student in the USA find a thesis advisor in departments that accept many PhD students, such as mathematics?
Answer: If a student has been accepted in a Ph.d. program, the faculty has already determined that there will be an advisor who will articulate with the student's research interests. Otherwise the student would not have been admitted. This emphasizes the extreme importance for a prospective Ph.d. student to do thorough research on prospective Ph.d. programs and their faculty. Only when there is a solid match between the research interests of the prospective student and the program faculty will the student be competitive for admission. (Of course they must also have a stellar academic record).
